title: Andrzejak-2012-nonrandomness-10.1103/physreve.86.046206
description: This dataset is a lossless BIDS (iEEG-BIDS) re-packaging of the Bern-Barcelona EEG database, containing 7500 pairs of focal and non-focal intracranial EEG signals from five patients with pharmacoresistant temporal lobe epilepsy. Each pair is a 20-second segment sampled at 512 Hz, pooled anonymously under a single pseudo-subject. The data support studies of nonrandomness, nonlinear dependence, and nonstationarity in epileptic EEG, and for distinguishing focal from non-focal signals.
methods_description: Long-term intracranial strip and depth electrode recordings (AD-TECH) were made at the University of Bern. The source applied a 0.5-150 Hz zero-phase Butterworth band-pass filter, downsampling to 512 Hz, and median re-referencing. Focal channels were those showing the first ictal changes, as judged by visual inspection. Randomly drawn 20-s windows from neighbouring channel pairs were stored as text, and were converted here to BrainVision IEEE float32 without filtering, resampling or rescaling.
